text: "What help you have given to the powerless! What mighty deliverance for the arm without strength!
What counsel you have offered to one without wisdom! And what abundance of insight you have displayed!
With whose help have you spoken these words? And whose breath was it that came out of you?
The shades below writhe in terror—the waters and all who dwell in them.

versions.text: The dead tremble beneath the waters, they and all who dwell there.
versions.explanation: רְפָאִים refers to the shades of the departed, and וְשֹׁכְנֵיהֶם most naturally attaches to "the waters and their inhabitants" rather than to the dead. The current rendering slightly blurs both points; the suggested line keeps the parallel structure and remains readable aloud.

text: Sheol lies naked before him, and Destruction has no covering.
He stretches out the north over the void and hangs the earth upon nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst beneath their weight.
He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his cloud across it.

versions.text: He covers the face of the moon, spreading his cloud across it.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כֶּסֶה most likely denotes the full moon (the same term used in Ps 81:3/Prov 7:20); adding "full" reflects the term more precisely without lengthening the line unduly. (Some read the consonants as "throne," which could be noted in a footnote.)

text: He has drawn a circle on the face of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven shudder, astonished at his rebuke.
By his power he stilled the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his breath the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
And these are but the fringes of his ways—only a whisper of a word do we hear of him. Who then could comprehend the thunder of his mighty deeds?

versions.text: And these are but the fringes of his ways—only a whisper of him do we hear. Who then could comprehend the thunder of his power?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "a whisper of a word" (שֵׁמֶץ דָּבָר), and the qere גְּבוּרוֹתָיו is plural, "mighty deeds/acts of power." The revision keeps the rhetorical force while matching the text more closely.
